method: Literal decimal arrays and asserted parameter/count/loss values extracted from the pinned C++ test source; no C++ was built or executed. Positions are literal f64; f64 raw intensity and f32 container intensity bits are retained separately. Fit parameter goldens were asserted through f32 metadata arrays. Training counts for second units follow the identical index selection as minute units. Loss goldens use raw f64 input intensities and fitted parameters rounded to f32; they are not the training loss.
derived_training_oracles: emg_training.tsv records ordered indices, initial mean and initial raw loss from an independent Python translation of source helper rules; source test directly asserts four training counts and four means. emg_gradient_review.json records independent derivative checks, not upstream test assertions.

class_test_review.literal_extraction: All seven literal traces, the four fit parameter sets per trace, the four output counts, the four Loss_function goldens, the four training counts, the four initial means, the three iRprop+ update cases, the three compute_z values, the six emg_point values and the applyEstimatedParameters endpoint are reproduced. docs/EMG_SUPPORT.md cites the Rust test and one asserted value per section.

source_anchors.operation: compute_z is (1/sqrt(2)) * (sigma/tau - (x-mu)/sigma); its sign and the constant 6.71e7 select which of the three EMG expressions is evaluated, and the comparison z <= 6.71e7 is inclusive

the middle emg_point branch evaluates exp(z*z) * erfc(z) directly up to z == 6.71e7; it overflows to infinity near z == 27, long before that threshold. The port preserves the expression and reports the non-finite result instead of substituting a scaled complementary error function
Loss_function divides each squared residual by xs.size() before accumulating, rather than summing and dividing once; the per-point division order is preserved
iRpropPlus caps the learning rate at 2000.0 where the iRprop+ paper recommends 50, grows it by 1.2 and shrinks it by 0.5; the source comment records the deviation
on a zero gradient with a zero previous gradient the update is -param_lr, so an exactly zero gradient still decreases the parameter by the learning rate; the class test asserts this case explicitly
sigma is initialised to mu * 1e-2 and tau to sigma * 2, both derived from the absolute initial mean, which is why the same peak in minutes and in seconds fits to different parameters
every learning rate starts at 0.0125, the value the iRprop+ paper recommends
computeMuMaxDistance is called with the training positions TrX, not the input; training always keeps both input endpoints, so for strictly increasing input the two spans are equal

the termination criterion is the population standard deviation of the last ten sampled losses falling below 1.0, sampled every 50th iteration into a ring initially filled with zeros; both magic values are carried over literally

the loop is while (++iter_idx <= max_gd_iter_) and the function returns iter_idx afterwards, so exhausting the limit reports one more than the number of evaluated iterations; the native estimate reports the evaluated count

a non-finite parameter or loss breaks out of the loop and the function returns the best iterate reached so far; the native API returns an error instead, because a silently truncated fit is indistinguishable from a converged one

after each update h is clamped below by the observed maximum intensity, mu to the initial mean plus or minus 0.35 of the training span, sigma to [1e-4, 20] and tau to [sigma, 15*sigma]; the last three are marked NOTE: magic value in the source
applyEstimatedParameters divides by xs.size() - 1 to get the average sampling step, so a single-point input divides by zero; the port requires two points whenever extrapolation is enabled

extrapolation extends only the side with the higher modelled endpoint, stopping at the opposite endpoint's intensity, at 1e-3, or once the added side exceeds three times the opposite side's distance from the apex
computeInitialMean advances one shared pair of indices across all six intensity percentages, so each level continues from where the previous one stopped rather than rescanning
extractTrainingSet computes derivatives only when i > 1, so a second sample already above the 80% threshold suppresses the whole derivative pass and leaves only the two endpoints in training

fitEMGPeakModel narrows each modelled intensity to float with a static_cast and appends a four-element emg_parameters FloatDataArray regardless of the peak count; the port checks the narrowing and returns the parameters typed instead
left_pos and right_pos are used as ternary conditions, so 0.0 means 'no bound' and a literal zero boundary cannot be expressed; the port uses Option<f64>

target_verification.note: The header, implementation and class test are byte-identical at both revisions; their sha256 values were recomputed from the pinned bc9cc12 checkout and match the values recorded here.
